The integral computes the optical depth along the path from the source to $\mathbf{x}$ [S1].

The claim states that the integral computes the optical depth along the path from the source to x. The evidence in Source [S1], specifically Equation (6), shows the propagator G containing the term exp(-∫₀ˢ c(x - w*(s - s')) ds'). In radiative transfer, the integral of the extinction coefficient (here denoted as c(x) or absorption coefficient a(x)) along the path represents the optical depth. The exponential of the negative of this integral represents the attenuation due to this optical depth. Therefore, the integral within the exponent indeed computes the optical depth along the straight-line path from the source position x' to the observation point x.
